title: A live-cell metabolic phenotyping platform for rapid phenotypic evaluation of high-producing Streptomyces aureofaciens strains through intracellular tetracycline fluorescence imaging
authors: Huaidong Zhang; Wen Yin; Liu He; Lijun Guo; Pingping Yang; Rongbin Zhao; Yufeng Cai; Haoran Chen; Fan Cai; Li Li; Qin Li; Jianzhong Huang
abstract: Abstract Background Efficient screening and evaluation of high-producing strains are essential for improving microbial cell factories, particularly for industrial production of valuable secondary metabolites. However, conventional strain screening strategies mainly rely on destructive fermentation sampling and chromatographic quantification, which are time-consuming and provide limited information regarding intracellular metabolic states. Therefore, rapid and non-invasive phenotypic approaches capable of monitoring metabolite accumulation at the single-cell level are highly desirable. Results We developed a live-cell metabolic phenotyping platform that enables rapid evaluation of tetracycline-producing Streptomyces aureofaciens strains through intracellular fluorescence imaging. The platform integrates a tetracycline-responsive molecular beacon with cell-penetrating peptide-assisted intracellular delivery, allowing visualization of intracellular tetracycline accumulation in living intact cells without cell lysis or metabolite extraction. The fluorescence response exhibited a concentration-dependent correlation with tetracycline production and reflected dynamic changes in intracellular antibiotic accumulation during fermentation. By applying this imaging-based phenotyping strategy to different industrial S. aureofaciens strains, high-producing strains were efficiently distinguished according to their intracellular fluorescence signatures. Importantly, fluorescence-based strain ranking showed agreement with HPLC quantification and was further validated through fermentation experiments. Conclusions This study establishes a non-destructive live-cell metabolic phenotyping platform for the phenotypic evaluation and prioritization of industrial microbial strains. By converting intracellular metabolite accumulation into a measurable optical phenotype, this strategy provides cellular-level information complementary to conventional analytical methods and offers a phenotypic prioritization tool that can facilitate microbial cell factory development.

title: Smart Biosensing Materials Enabled by Artificial Intelligence: From Material Design to AI-Assisted Sensing
authors: Shikuan Shao; Xiaohu Xia
venue: AI-Integrated Biosensors, Microfluidics, and Wearable Systems for Personalized Healthcare
abstract: Abstract Modern biosensors increasingly rely on smart biosensing materials that translate target recognition and interfacial interactions into measurable optical, catalytic, electrical, thermal, or multimodal signals. The performance of these materials depends on precise control of structural, compositional, and surface properties, as well as assay and biointerface conditions that determine how material-level functions are translated into analytical performance. Because these interconnected factors are often optimized by trial-and-error experimentation, the development of high-performance sensing materials can be time-consuming, resource-intensive, and difficult to generalize. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), offers new opportunities to advance biosensing materials research by learning structure-property-performance relationships from experimental and computational data. In addition to guiding materials discovery, design, and synthesis optimization, AI is increasingly being used to interpret complex sensing outputs and extract information from machine-readable signals. In this chapter, we discuss the emerging interface between AI and smart biosensing materials. We first examine the data foundation required for AI-assisted materials development, including data sources, curation, and representations. We then summarize predictive AI tools and design workflows for materials optimization and discovery. Next, we highlight sensing materials engineered to generate information-rich outputs for AI-assisted signal interpretation. Finally, we provide an outlook on automated and self-driving platforms that may integrate materials development, biosensing, and decision-making within closed-loop workflows.

title: AI-Integrated Wearable Closed-Loop Diagnostic and Therapeutic Systems
authors: Xuejia Kang; Peizhen Sun
venue: AI-Integrated Biosensors, Microfluidics, and Wearable Systems for Personalized Healthcare
abstract: Abstract Wearable healthcare is undergoing a transition from passive monitoring toward closed-loop diagnostic, therapeutic, and theragnostic systems. Conventional open-loop care relies on intermittent measurements and delayed treatment adjustment, whereas closed-loop systems continuously sense physiological or biochemical states, interpret those signals, deliver or guide intervention, and evaluate response. In wearable medicine, this transition is enabled by skin-interfaced sensors, flexible electronics, microneedles, bioresponsive materials, artificial intelligence, adaptive control, and miniaturized actuation modules. This chapter reviews artificial intelligence-integrated wearable closed-loop systems from conceptual foundations to application domains. We distinguish open-loop, feedback-assisted, and closed-loop systems; classify wearable architectures into self-sustained material/bioresponse-driven systems, externally triggered electronics/control-driven systems, and hybrid material-electronic systems; and organize the field into diagnostic loops, therapeutic loops, and integrated theragnostic loops. Application domains include wearable closed-loop drug delivery and metabolic control, smart bandages and adaptive wound therapy, wearable neuromodulation and adaptive transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, closed-loop sensorimotor restoration through brain-computer interface-functional electrical stimulation, electromyography-functional electrical stimulation, and bidirectional prosthetics, and wearable biofeedback systems for sleep, stress, fatigue, and autonomic regulation. Across domains, the central challenge is not simply whether sensors and artificial intelligence models can generate accurate outputs, but whether the complete sensor-algorithm-actuator-feedback pathway is valid, safe, interpretable, and clinically meaningful.

title: Smart Apparel for Continuous Healthcare Monitoring: Textile Biosensing, AI-Driven Design, and Digital Manufacturing
authors: Jia Wu; Yurou Zeng; Pengyu Chen
venue: AI-Integrated Biosensors, Microfluidics, and Wearable Systems for Personalized Healthcare
abstract: Abstract Smart apparel is evolving beyond apparel with electronic components attached to it into a wearable healthcare platform in which textiles, conductive materials, biosensors, electronic modules, data processing, and apparel design are developed as an integrated system. This chapter reviews the role of smart apparel in continuous health monitoring with emphasis on textile-based sensing and apparel-level integration. It first discusses conductive polymers, fibers, and yarns as the material basis for sensing and signal transmission. It then examines major integration strategies, including functional components built into textile structures, deposited onto textile surfaces, or attached as flexible electronic modules. The chapter further describes how apparel-integrated biosystems convert physiological and biochemical signals into usable health information, and how AI-assisted design and digital manufacturing can connect material selection, sensor placement, body fit, and scalable production workflows. This chapter shows how smart apparel opens a new healthcare paradigm by turning daily apparel into an active interface for continuous monitoring, interpretation, and timely care.
